title: Correct deterministic scoring and add comprehensive tests
objective: Correct the deterministic classifier and scoring semantics within schema v2, and establish a comprehensive pytest suite covering the analysis, collector parser, storage/export, validation, and degraded-path contracts.
forbidden_changes: Do not change schema v2, collection/storage/export public interfaces, source modes, workflows, frontend, dependencies, docs, or orchestration control files.
Do not silently weaken privacy or degraded-state validation to make a test pass.
Do not introduce an LLM or probabilistic classifier; the engine remains deterministic and documented.
Do not modify or merge into the default branch.
deliverables: Post deduplication by stable identity before sector analysis
Correct intent matching that avoids overlapping-keyword double counting and deterministic tie handling
Consistent non-spam scoring denominators and explicit spam behavior
Removal of unused activity output or a contract-compatible resolution that does not change files outside scope
Honest null buy/sell ratio when there are buys but zero sells, with deterministic zero/zero behavior

Pytest coverage for classifier/scoring thresholds and formulas, malformed/empty data, parser row alignment, storage LKG, schema/privacy export, timezone boundary, forced failure, and explicit simulation labels
Atomic implementation commit and handoff report
acceptance_criteria: Spam records never enter newbie counts, purity counts, sentiment, intent, or denominators.
Duplicate post identities are counted once per sector and ordering is deterministic.
A buy count above zero with sell count zero exports buy_sell_ratio=null; zero buys and zero sells has a documented deterministic value covered by tests.
Scoring weights and interpretation boundaries have direct unit tests, including 0, 20, 40, 60, and 75.
Guba parser, LKG preservation, schema validation, public privacy, Shanghai day boundary, unavailable source, and explicit simulation behaviors are tested without live network access.
The full suite passes on Python 3.11 and changes remain inside declared write scope.
